title: Artwork and Dieline Checklist for Packaging
excerpt: Learn how to prepare packaging artwork with dielines, bleed, safe area, CMYK, Pantone colors, barcode and final approval.
coverAlt: Box dieline with fold lines and dimensions for artwork planning

sections.heading: Use the correct dieline
sections.body: A dieline shows cut lines, crease lines, glue area, bleed and safe area. It must match the approved packaging size and structure.

sections.heading: Keep important text inside safe area
sections.body: Logo, barcode, ingredients, product details and important text should stay inside the safe area to avoid trimming or folding issues.

sections.heading: Prepare CMYK or Pantone colors
sections.body: CMYK is common for full color printing, while Pantone colors may be used for exact brand colors or special spot color printing.

sections.heading: Check barcode and spelling
sections.body: Before final approval, customers should check barcode size, spelling, legal text, product claims, ingredients and all design details.

faqs.question: Do I need a dieline for custom packaging?
faqs.answer: Yes. Final production should use an approved dieline that matches box size, structure, bleed and safe area.

faqs.question: Which file format is best for packaging artwork?
faqs.answer: Editable AI, PDF, EPS or high-quality print-ready files are commonly preferred for packaging production.
